prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching after state check and Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. SCADA Engineer: telemetry gaps. Shore Control Room: dispatch, keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis, authorization, handover record; Control Engineer verifies, reduces stepwise, no chasing fluctuations; on release confirms authorization, restores gradually. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; switching one action/step; restoration after Field Supervisor clear. Failure: pause, safe state. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Personnel reconciliation (each shore/vessel/work-location movement): Marine Coordinator sets expected count/destination; counts separate per vessel/location, CTV and Daughter Craft independent; Vessel Master verifies aboard before departure; North/South Access Scanner record access events; Personnel Tracking Console keeps count, uses count correction→verified personnel total (only after reason recorded); checks at departure/arrival/intermediate, before work and before return departure. Discrepancy unresolved until all accounted: Marine Coordinator pauses transfers, informs Shore Control Room, escalates to Duty Planner with time; Vessel Master safe position;

New part:
S585: Personnel movements do not resume until the Marine Coordinator confirms that the count is reconciled or an authorized response is in place.
S586: Any unresolved discrepancy and its control measures are included in the shift handover.
S587: Software changes are managed through a controlled lifecycle that protects the integrity and availability of operational systems.
S588: Each operational software component has an identified owner, approved version, and documented configuration baseline.
S589: The baseline records software versions, configuration parameters, dependencies, and applicable hardware revisions.
S590: Source code and configuration files are held in access-controlled repositories with revision history enabled.
S591: Changes are developed and reviewed outside the live operational environment.
S592: Release packages are built from approved source and checked for completeness, integrity, and compatibility.
S593: The SCADA Engineer uses the Firmware Hash Attestation to verify the approved image before loading a release.
S594: The Control Engineer confirms that proposed changes have a clear operational purpose and defined scope.
S595: Technical approval is recorded before a change is scheduled for deployment to an operational system.
S596: Reviewers assess safety effects, cybersecurity risks, interfaces, and the impact on ongoing maintenance activities.
S597: Changes affecting protection functions or control behavior receive additional engineering scrutiny.
S598: Testing is performed in a representative test environment before operational acceptance is considered.
S599: The SCADA Gateway is checked for compatibility with the approved software and configuration baseline.
S600: The Turbine Controller is tested against defined operating limits and expected fault responses.
S601: The Pitch System is verified to retain its approved control behavior after an applicable software change.
S602: The Converter Cabinet is checked for expected communication and protection behavior during regression testing.
S603: Changes affecting the Offshore Substation are reviewed for consequences to the safe operation of connected equipment.
S604: The Main Transformer protection settings remain subject to their separate engineering approval process.
S605: The Cybersecurity Gateway is assessed for continued compliance with access controls and security requirements.
S606: The Shore Control Room confirms that monitoring and operator procedures remain suitable for the revised configuration.
S607: Deployment is scheduled for an approved maintenance window with qualified personnel available to supervise the work.
S608: A rollback method is documented and checked before deployment begins.
S609: If verification fails, the change is stopped and the affected system is returned to its last approved baseline where practicable.
S610: Configuration records are updated after successful deployment, including the approval evidence, test results, and installed version.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
